Key findings

Computed automatically from this run's own tables, so they always match the details below. Associations, not causes.

Unusual moves after strict correction
8 of 441 tests

Holm-adjusted (all 441 event x stock x window tests at once); 10 with the serial-correlation-robust (HAC) version. Largest: EVT019 ADANI_ENTERPRISES -75.6% (CAR_-5_+5); EVT019 ADANI_PORTS -46.4% (CAR_-5_+5); EVT007 ADANI_ENTERPRISES -44.1% (CAR_-5_+5). Significant means unusual for the market model, not caused by the event.

Average reaction across the 21 events
-0.12%

Mean CAR over Day -1 to +1 across 21 events and all seven stocks; 95% cluster-bootstrap interval -0.53% to +0.49%. Tests that allow for event-day volatility and same-day correlation: BMP p = 0.915, Kolari-Pynnonen p = 0.927, rank test p = 0.610. Positive and negative events cancel, so the average says little on its own.

Results days: 266 company announcements
2.7x normal variance

Over Day -1 to +1 a company's own results move its stock 2.7 times as much (in variance) as an ordinary 3-day stretch (95% interval 2.2 to 3.2; about 1.02 expected with no effect). Average |CAR| 2.90%. The signed average is -0.28% (BMP p = 0.130), as expected without beat/miss data. The volatility effect appears in both the development and holdout years for 2 of 7 stocks. On ordinary mid-quarter days (placebo, 30 sessions later) the same measure is 0.9 (0.7 to 1.1), so fat tails alone do not explain it.

HAC-Holm significant results by event window. Wider windows add noise, so fewer moves stand out; a result that holds in only one window is fragile.

Average reaction across events (CAAR)

For each event, abnormal returns are averaged over the chosen stocks, then averaged over events and added up from Day −5. The shaded band is a 95% cluster-bootstrap interval that resamples whole groups of related events. Groups with fewer than three independent clusters get no band. Pooled averages describe association, not cause.

Compare event classes, sectors and stocks

Mean CAR across events for the CAR window chosen above. Sector and stock rows use all events. Most sectors contain one stock, so a sector row mostly shows that one stock. Sector labels are this project's broad grouping, not an official classification.

Robust group tests (BMP, Kolari-Pynnönen, rank)

Group-level tests for the CAR window chosen above. BMP standardizes each CAR and uses the observed spread across events, so extra event-day volatility does not create false signals. Kolari-Pynnönen further shrinks BMP when stocks share the same event day (their residuals move together). The rank test uses ranks instead of raw returns, so one extreme day cannot drive it. Variance ratio = average squared standardized CAR: about 1 when nothing unusual happens.

Company results days (issuer-level earnings study)

Every quarterly results announcement of the seven companies from Q1 FY17 to Q2 FY26, each studied only for the company that reported. Dates come from board-meeting histories and dated news reports (results/earnings_events.csv lists a source for each). Day 0 is the first session on or after the announcement date. Without analyst forecasts we cannot tell a beat from a miss, so the main measure is how much the stock moves, not in which direction.

Inference & uncertainty

Confidence intervals and Holm-adjusted p-values are approximate under the current model assumptions. Statistical significance is not causality.

Estimation-window robustness

The market model is re-fit with 60, 100, and 150 pre-event sessions while keeping the 20-session gap and event windows fixed. Holm correction is performed separately within each specification. Treat changes as sensitivity, not a search for the most significant result.

How the event-window choice changes conclusions

Same events and stocks, three window lengths. Wider windows can capture slower reactions but also add more days of unrelated news and noise.

Robustness evidence ledger

Lists findings that are HAC-Holm significant in at least one estimation-window specification. “Stable” means significant in all three tested lengths; event overlap, shared episodes, and timing/source cautions are shown separately. Stable significance does not establish causality.

Across-stock consistency

Do stocks move in the same direction around this event?

Hypothetical trading diagnostic

Hypothetical, exploratory rule; not an investable backtest and not live trading performance.

Holdout uncertainty

Cluster-bootstrap intervals resample dependent event clusters. A holdout interval that crosses zero does not establish a reliable excess-return edge. Excess returns are in percentage points (pp) versus NIFTY 50.

Warning: the holdout 95% interval includes zero (-0.26 to +0.38 pp). The data are consistent with no excess return; no reliable trading edge is established.

Do patterns repeat on unseen events?

Patterns measured on the development events (2016 to Feb 2023) are checked on the later holdout events (Oct 2023 to 2025). Event classes have very few events in each sample, so these checks have little power: "no" means the pattern did not repeat, and "yes" is not proof.

Event headline classifier (NLP)

A TF-IDF + logistic regression model is trained on real, sourced news headlines to label an event headline as one of six classes. It is checked on held-out groups of related headlines and on this project's 21 registry headlines, which are never used for training. It is a cross-check on the hand-assigned categories, not a replacement.

Event register

Event dependence & independence audit

Temporal overlap is calculated on trading sessions. Shared episode IDs and categories are metadata-based clustering warnings—not evidence of causality. Pending source/timing checks remain review cautions.

Event timing sensitivity

For unresolved timing, compare plausible session alignments. If the context indicates an after-market/evening release, the first scenario is strictly the next available session—never the same-day close that preceded publication. For other uncertain timestamps, compare the first session on/after the date with the following session. This is a robustness diagnostic, not an automatic date correction.

Realized volatility before vs after events

Realized stock and benchmark volatility use non-overlapping trading-session windows −20:−1 and +1:+20, excluding Day 0. Annualization uses √252. Event-window market-model residual volatility is shown separately and is not the same as realized stock volatility.

Category-level evidence

Category summaries average stocks within each event and then aggregate within episodes. Overlapping event windows are excluded. A category needs at least three independent episodes to receive a numeric summary; “insufficient independent episodes” is an honest data limitation, not a zero effect.

Data provenance & interpretation limits

Both stocks and the benchmark use the Close field, so both sides are measured on the same price basis. These are price returns: dividends are excluded on both sides, so this is not a total shareholder return comparison.
Daily data cannot isolate intraday reactions to market-hours announcements. The sample contains only a small, hand-selected set of events; overlapping news and shared macro episodes weaken independence. Do not interpret these associations as causal effects or future returns.
